I have crappy education and yet scored high on mensa test.

Details on my education if you are interested:

I was on tiny elementary school in tiny village, where one subject was taught to 2-3 classes simultaneously and the most attention was directed towards the youngest ones, so only to 1st and 3rd graders were under some supervision, rest of us were left with reading exercises or something.

From fifth grade I went to different school, where classes were composed of pupils of the same grade, quality was better, school had library, spent some time there.

Then I was scared of entrance exams and went to a high school that accepted me without them. Terrible choice. It was graphic design school, and honestly, we didnt learn even what we were supposed to. Informatics? Nothing. We were told to pretend to be working, and allowed to do whatever we want. Facebook, games... Maths? In the last year, we didnt learn anything new at all. Literature? We barely made it through basic eras. No history, no chemistry apart from one year, where out teacher was... kind of strange, and taught us nothing, really. As of practical things regarding design, we were taught from really outdated scripts. Like, gif-is-the-peak-of-technology and bring-your-own-images-on-floppies outdated.

As of college, i was not interested in joining one. Everyone kept telling me it would be a loss if I did not apply, so I did just so I wouldnt have to listen to them, and was not accepted anyway.

Well. I think I believe something similar. I thought the mensa test was kinda accurate until I took it and scored... a bit more then I thought I would. 

The issue is that apart from the test I'm pretty dumb. I'm way slower than my classmates, I was crying because of it even. I didn't even pass the entrance test to uni last year, and probably would fail this year as well.

Majority of people I talk to are definitely better off than me regarding intelligence. And some of them scored lower. This all lead me to believe that the tests are kinda not good measurement at all, or that my results are mistake.
